input.query: College Promise Program tuition what it covers

results.response:
The Promise Program covers **100% of in-state tuition** for eligible students working toward an Associate in Arts (AA), Associate in Science (AS), or Associate in Applied Science (AAS). It's a **"last-dollar" scholarship**, meaning it kicks in after federal aid like the Pell Grant and scholarships like Bright Futures have been applied.

What it does **not** cover: lab fees, distance learning fees, books, and supplies.

A few other basics to keep in mind:
1. You must be enrolled at least **12 credits** per term.
2. You must stay on track with the College's Financial Aid Satisfactory Academic Progress (GPA and completion rate) to keep the funding.
3. There are **no GPA or income requirements**.
4. Bachelor's degrees are not covered.

You can read the full details on the [Promise Program page](https://irsc.edu/admissions/promise/) and the [Financial Aid FAQ](https://irsc.edu/admissions/financial-aid/faqs/).

The P.E.R.T. (Postsecondary Education Readiness Test) is the College's placement test that measures your reading, writing, and math skill levels so you can be placed into the right courses. It's strongly encouraged and required unless you qualify for an exemption.

To schedule it:
1. Go to the [P.E.R.T. testing page](https://irsc.edu/programs/academic-resources-support/assessment-centers/pert-test/), which has a tab for each campus (Massey–Fort Pierce, Pruitt–Port St. Lucie, Chastain–Stuart, Mueller–Vero Beach, Dixon Hendry–Okeechobee).

Dual enrollment at Indian River State College lets you earn both high school credit and college credit for the same course while you're still working toward your diploma. There are three main types:

1. **Academic** – earn credit toward an Associate or Baccalaureate degree (part or full time); requires passing an entry level exam.
2. **Career/Technical** – earn credit toward an Associate degree or Technical certificate.
3. **Early Admission** – for highly qualified students full-time in college after completing six semesters of secondary enrollment (grades 9–11).

To get placed in the right course, the College uses placement measures such as standardized test scores or strong high school coursework (an unweighted GPA of 3.0 with a "B" or better in qualifying classes), with transcripts and official score reports sent directly to The River. Courses are offered across the five College campuses and at many local high schools, including before, during, and after the school day and in summer. New dual enrollment students seeking an Associate in Arts degree are encouraged to complete SLS 1101 Student Success in their first semester.

For the full details, see the [Dual Enrollment program page](https://irsc.edu/programs/special-programs/dual-enrollment/) and the [Admissions – Dual Enrollment](https://irsc.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current/catalog/services-to-students/apply-for-admissions/admissions-dual-enrollment) section of the College catalog. There isn't actually an income threshold for Florida residency at Indian River State College. Residency is based on legal domicile, not income: you (or your parent/guardian, if you're a dependent) must have maintained legal Florida residency for **at least 12 consecutive months** before the first day of classes, and you must submit at least two documents, including one Tier 1 document (like a Florida driver's license, vehicle registration, voter registration, or proof of permanent full-time employment in Florida), plus the [Florida Residency Declaration (Form FRD-1)](https://irsc.edu/admissions/tuition-fees/residency-requirements/). Living in Florida or attending classes in Florida does not by itself count — that's set out under Florida Statute 1009.21 and SBOE Rule 6A-10.044, not an income test.

- **Financial aid** (Pell Grant, etc.) has its own income-based eligibility, which you check through the FAFSA, not the residency form.
